Revision: a41c380246d3d9f9874f0f792d234dc0cc17c180
License: 0BSD (LICENSE.txt); bundled dependencies retain their own licenses.

Vendored source including bundled dependencies. Built for A64 by nixe-cpu-jit.

Nixe adaptations:
- backend/exception_handler{.h,_posix.cpp}: expose cold fault resolution and
  allow nixe to own POSIX signal capture (DYNARMIC_EXTERNAL_FAULT_HANDLER).
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64.cpp: check halt/budget at linked and indirect/return
  transitions so scheduler preemption and memory transitions remain bounded.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/sys_dc.cpp: end blocks after cache operations;
  nixe applies ownership transitions after dropping its execution lease.
- ir/opt/a64_get_set_elimination_pass.cpp, ir/opt/passes.h and
  both A64 backends: retain setters visible at memory-abort exits
  while still forwarding register values and eliminating redundant accesses.
- interface/A64/config.h, frontend/A64/translate and both A64 backends:
  optionally stop at unknown extension HINTs instead of silently dropping their
  semantics on newer guest CPUs.
- interface/A64/pointer_authentication.h, A64 decoding/translation, IR and host
  crypto emitters: implement QARMA5-based FEAT_PAuth2 with immutable process keys,
  PAC/AUT/XPAC, PACGA, authenticated branches/returns and authenticated loads.
  Pointer widths match the execution address space, with TBI=0 and no FPAC.
- A64 host entry points, indirect dispatch and return handlers: validate execution
  addresses before the location hash drops high PC bits, including cached
  indirect branches, returns and entry from the host.
- common/crypto/qarma.{cpp,h}: QARMA5 helper adapted from QEMU's
  target/arm/tcg/pauth_helper.c (Linaro copyright, LGPL-2.1-or-later).
  Its license is retained in LICENSE.qarma.txt; the original vendored files keep
  their existing licenses.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/load_store_atomic.cpp: LSE atomic operations
  adapted from Lichii revision 21d62e43caa178aeb04e74585b3aad622b278b84
  (src/dynarmic/src/dynarmic/frontend/A64/translate/impl/load_store_atomic.cpp).
  The file retains its GPL-3.0-or-later notice. CPU feature selection enables
  LSE at translation time; exclusive IR implements CAS/CASP, SWP and atomic ALU
  operations, including acquire/release and retries without partial register
  updates. LDAPR uses the existing limited-order acquire memory operations,
  gated by the RCpc CPU feature. A64CheckMemoryAlignment in both host backends
  faults before a misaligned atomic operation; precise memory exits preserve
  earlier setters.

The Rust/C ABI integration is in crates/cpu-jit. The generic native fault
capture implementation is shared with the interpreter in cpu-direct-memory.
